best_parts: node end_probe: end-artery probe (gangrene and perforation because it is an end artery) with two TR4 chain-reversal traps; the only node in S2 that tests the 'why the end artery matters' part of O3
node age_t2: 'Either one; age makes no difference' is a distinct TR15 model (age-blind), refuted by the age-linked cause in the feedback
node pain_ok: skip lane to chain_probe after a correct first answer (expertise-reversal path), with teach_pain kept for the slow path
flaws: node age_probe: the stem names both candidate blocks ('a swollen lymphoid wall, or a hard faecolith') and then gives the cue 'viral illness'; the key is findable by matching words, which weakens the TR15 trap
node chain_hint: 'Which tissue, lining the abdominal wall, can point to a spot?' all but names the parietal peritoneum; a hint should narrow, not hand over the answer
node end_probe: the key is the longest option and the only one with a 'since' justification; key findable by form (DP1)
node vig_probe: the key is the only 'Gastroenteritis' option and the only one with a because-clause; key findable by form (DP1)
node pain_hint: asks which region T10 covers, a question off the pain-course probe it supports; the hint does not connect to the choice
node sym_probe: 'Fever, then pain, then vomiting' is dominated; no one holding Murphy's sequence at any level picks it over vomiting-first
TR15 is probed once in S2 (age_probe) with no mirror probe in the adult; the trap is not re-tested within the segment

best_parts: node pain_hint: two-step hint ('Which layer has to be inflamed before pain can point to one spot?') that narrows toward the parietal peritoneum without naming it
node adult_probe / adult_t15: mirror probe of the child case with the age reversed (45-year-old, faecolith); tests TR15 in a second form, the reversal the trap map asks for
node mech_probe: localisation probe in which every wrong option is a named TR4 model (rising pressure over-stimulates T10; ischaemia first), so the path reveals which wrong model the learner holds
flaws: node s6: the key 'Less likely: the vomiting came before the pain' is the only 'Less likely' option, so the key is findable by direction (DP1)

node c3: option 'Arterial compromise, rising pressure, venous congestion, gangrene' starts with a step no one with obstruction-first knowledge would place first; dominated (DP2); the stem also says 'Obstruction comes first and perforation last', leaving the middle four to guess
node sym_probe: 'Fever, then pain, then vomiting' is dominated (DP2)
node chain_teach: the whole obstruction-to-gangrene chain is explained before the learner predicts any step; ask-before-tell is broken for O3 (R1)
O3 'say why the end artery matters' is taught in wx4 and not probed anywhere on the path; no end-artery probe exists in S2
no fast lane: pain_ok and every correct reply go straight into teaching, so an expert cannot skip (R5)
node age_hint: 'Which tissue is abundant in this 9-year-old's appendix?' leads straight to lymphoid tissue; hint leaks the answer
node pain_probe and mech_probe use 'Tempting:' openers in feedback almost every time; formulaic voice across the segment

best_parts: node c2: venous-before-arterial probe placed after a worked case; each trap maps to TR4 with its own feedback (c2t1, c2t2) and a 'show me why' branch
node c3t: sure_note 'slow down: the dramatic events are the end of the chain, not its start' names the confident-error model well
node wx4d: 'deeper' branch on why an end artery matters (no backup route), the one place this variant explains O3's end-artery reason
flaws: node start: the first probe is binary (faecolith vs lymphoid), with a 'cold' cue that points to the answer; the TR15 trap gets one option and no second form
nodes wx1 to wx4: the full chain is told as a worked case before any probe; ask-before-tell is broken for the mechanism (R1)
no end-artery probe anywhere in S2; the O3 'why the end artery matters' claim is taught only
node c3: 'Arterial compromise, rising pressure, venous congestion, gangrene' is dominated (DP2), and both trap options route to the same feedback node c3t, so they diagnose no separate model
node s6: the key is the only 'Less likely' option, so it is findable by direction (DP1)
node s5: 'Fever, then pain, then vomiting' is dominated (DP2)
node c3h and c2h: hints ask 'the veins or the arteries?' with a two-way choice that gives the answer away
no fast lane and no mirror probe for TR15 in S2; learners cannot skip the worked case

b's two-step pain_hint in place of a's pain_hint and chain_hint, so hints narrow without naming the answer
